direction: Epistasis-decomposed beam search with cascading funnel scoring
rationale: This combines three of the strongest concepts: (1) epistasis-aware sparse decomposition reduces the combinatorial space by factoring the problem into weakly-interacting clusters, (2) adaptive beam search provides an efficient and GPU-friendly search within and across clusters, and (3) the cascading funnel (ESM-2 -> ProteinMPNN -> RaSP) ensures high-quality scoring without excessive computational cost. This direction is the most practically implementable within the 15-minute constraint and requires no custom model training — all components use pretrained models off the shelf.
first_step: Implement the single-mutant prescreening with ESM-2: load ESM-2 650M, compute masked marginal log-likelihood ratios for all 19 substitutions at each position, rank positions by max improvement. This is the foundation that all downstream search methods build upon. Benchmark: should process a 300-residue protein in under 30 seconds on A100.
expected_signal: For proteins in the Mega-scale dataset, the ESM-2 single-mutant ranking should achieve Spearman rho > 0.4 with experimental ddG values. The top-50 positions should contain >80% of positions where experimental stabilizing mutations exist. This validates the pre-screening stage before building the full pipeline.

direction: Game-theoretic equilibrium search with GNN epistasis priors
rationale: This direction bridges game theory and structural biology in a novel way. The game-theoretic framework (inspired by GameOpt, ICLR 2025) provides a principled decomposition of the combinatorial problem into per-position decisions, while the GNN locality prior (inspired by Stability Oracle and AlphaGMut) provides structurally informed coupling between positions. Together they offer: (a) theoretical guarantees from game theory (convergence to equilibria), (b) data efficiency from structure-aware priors, and (c) a clean separation between position selection (which positions to mutate) and amino acid optimization (what to mutate to). This is more novel than beam search but slightly harder to implement.
first_step: Prototype the best-response dynamics optimizer: given k positions and a scorer, implement iterative best response where each position sequentially optimizes its amino acid choice while others are fixed. Test on 10 small Mega-scale proteins with k=4 positions, comparing convergence rate and solution quality vs exhaustive enumeration (19^4 = 130K, feasible for validation).
expected_signal: Best-response dynamics should converge within 5-10 sweeps for k=4 positions. The equilibrium solution should be within 5% of the exhaustive optimum in predicted ddG for >80% of test cases. Convergence should require <500 scorer calls vs 130K for exhaustive search (260x speedup). If convergence is slow or solution quality is poor, this indicates strong higher-order epistasis that defeats the best-response decomposition.

direction: Diffusion-guided mutation sampling with MCTS refinement
rationale: This is the most research-forward direction, combining two cutting-edge techniques: (1) guided diffusion sampling generates diverse, high-quality multi-mutant candidates in parallel, avoiding the sequential bottleneck of beam search, and (2) MCTS refinement explores local improvements around the best diffusion samples, combining the global exploration of diffusion with the local exploitation of tree search. This mirrors the MCTD-ME framework (Liu et al. 2025) but specialized for stability optimization rather than inverse folding. This direction has the highest potential ceiling but also the highest implementation complexity.
first_step: Implement a minimal guided diffusion sampler: take ESM-2, mask k positions in the input sequence, sample from the masked language model distribution with guidance from ProteinMPNN structure scores. Start without the MCTS component — just generate 256 samples per protein and rank by combined score. Benchmark diversity (unique sequences) and quality (top-1 predicted ddG) vs beam search on 20 proteins.
expected_signal: Diffusion sampling should produce >90% unique sequences (high diversity). The top-1 predicted ddG from 256 diffusion samples should match or exceed the beam search result (W=100, k steps) at comparable or lower computational cost. If diversity is low, increase guidance temperature. If quality is low, the guidance signal needs stronger coupling to the ProteinMPNN structure score.

direction: Multi-fidelity Bayesian optimization with position bandits
rationale: This direction combines bandit-based position selection with multi-fidelity Bayesian optimization, creating a fully adaptive pipeline that learns which positions matter and how to score them efficiently. Thompson sampling allocates evaluation budget to the most informative positions, while multi-fidelity BO (with ESM-2 as cheap fidelity and RaSP as expensive fidelity) maximizes information per evaluation dollar. This is the most principled approach from a decision-theoretic perspective, with the strongest theoretical foundations (Bayesian regret bounds from Qiu et al.), but requires a GP surrogate model that may struggle with the discrete, high-dimensional space.
first_step: Implement Thompson sampling for position selection: for N=50 candidate positions, maintain a Beta distribution posterior for each position's probability of appearing in the optimal k-mutation set. Run 100 rounds of exploration where each round evaluates a random mutation at the top-k sampled positions. Measure convergence of posterior beliefs and compare selected positions vs oracle-optimal positions.
expected_signal: After 100 rounds (100*k evaluations), the top-k positions by posterior mean should overlap >60% with the oracle-optimal positions (determined from exhaustive single-mutant evaluation). Thompson sampling should show faster convergence than uniform random position sampling. If convergence is slow, the position value distributions may be too similar, requiring a more discriminative scorer.
